I use computers a lot. I never really grew up with a father figure. No one has never really shown me how to build shit or repair stuff at home. My wife is excellent with stuff like this so I usually just make sure our router works.

My daughter is three years old. A couple of months ago she asked me if I could build stuff. I said yeah although I have never constructed anything in my whole life. She then asked me to build her something. I said that I had no idea what we could build, but perhaps we could try and fix her bicycle which has been broken for some time. We did it and afterwards she declared that I could build anything.

I said yeah and since then, honestly. I get stuff done and nails hammered into the wall because my kid told me that I could do it.

Don't really know if there's a lesson learned here except that kids make you do great things and often improves your life in ways you could never imagine.
I became a better person when my daughter told me that I could do anything.

I learned how the US political system worked by a video like that. House of Cards made a lot more sense afterwards.

I'm definitely a night owl, always have been. I like my peace and quiet and hate the hustle and bustle of the day. I work night shift during the week and get to drive on one of the busiest traffic corridors in the country with no traffic; my 25 minute commute would take well over an hour were it a day shift. No traffic, no lines, no yelling and screaming, just me and my thoughts. I get home from work in the morning and get to spend my free time in an empty house just reading, working out or messing around on the computer. I also live in the very beautiful pacific northwest overlooking the Puyallup River Valley and have the privilege of enjoying nature at it's best. Sunrise over the mountains, birds over the valley, trees as far as the eye can see, rolling hills. The day I have to move for work will be bittersweet, I don't know if I'll ever find a better place to live than this.

Early bird here! I have two favorite things. 1) The "Golden Hour" to me is the most beautiful part of the day. Everything seems a bit softer, quieter. 2) I love the feeling of being up and at 'em hours before most people are awake. Get my vitamin D in from the sun homes.

To be honest ive been both at certain points of my life. About a year ago I was a night owl, I loved the night because it brought a sense of isolation. With my family asleep I felt I could do the things I wanted to do in private, also, the conversations I tended to have with people late at night were at a much more intimate level which I enjoyed.

Currently do to certain types of medicine and restrictions I now have to wake up early. I love the peace early morning brings along with the freshness of starting a new day.

As a chronic insomniac i sometimes go for walks at 4-5am, the night life is usually over by then and during the summer this is when the birds start singing and the morning twilight begins.

It's always so quiet, no cars, no people, just me and the night time.

I also love seeing the stars, but living in a city makes that harder now, or at least less pretty as you can't see as many.

I'm both, I think. I usually stay up till midnight or 1AM and wake up around 7:30-8AM.

-Morning: I love the morning sun. There's something different about the way shadows are cast from east to West that just makes me content. I love the chill, crisp morning air as well. The other bonus is that a get to fully utilize all the time in the day. The happy little birds chirping also warms my heart.

-Night: Alone time. I get to do what I want, when I want. My roomates aren't eating as much internet bandwith. The quiet and calm is nice. I don't have to worry about any errands or anything because I've already got them done.
I'm a morning person, and I love when the sun first starts to light everything up but you can't see it. Feels like the world is waking up and anything is possible. That and my morning cup of coffee.

I love how in the early morning it's so peaceful and the air is crisp. It is a fresh new day, you can watch a beautiful sunrise and I love the fact that you get to enjoy all the tranquility whilst everyone else is snoring in bed.
